title: The LORD Is My Strength and My Shield

verses.text: To You, O LORD, I call; be not deaf to me, O my Rock. For if You remain silent, I will be like those descending to the Pit.
Hear my cry for mercy when I call to You for help, when I lift up my hands toward Your holy sanctuary.
Do not drag me away with the wicked, and with the workers of iniquity, who speak peace to their neighbors while malice is in their hearts.
Repay them according to their deeds and for their works of evil. Repay them for what their hands have done; bring back on them what they deserve.
Since they show no regard for the works of the LORD or what His hands have done, He will tear them down and never rebuild them.
Blessed be the LORD, for He has heard my cry for mercy.
The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusts in Him, and I am helped. Therefore my heart rejoices, and I give thanks to Him with my song.
The LORD is the strength of His people, a stronghold of salvation for His anointed.
Save Your people and bless Your inheritance; shepherd them and carry them forever.

context.author: The title says “of David” (Hebrew le-David), which can mean by David, for David or about David. Seventy-three psalms carry his name; tradition and the New Testament take many of them as his.
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship in Jerusalem, and every reader who prays
context.setting: “To You, O LORD, I call; be not deaf to me, O my Rock. For if You remain silent, I will be like those descending to the Pit” (v.1). David lifts his hands “toward Your holy sanctuary” (v.2) and asks not to be dragged away with the wicked, “who speak peace to their neighbors while malice is in their hearts” (v.3). Then the answer comes: “Blessed be the LORD, for He has heard my cry for mercy” (v.6). “The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusts in Him, and I am helped” (v.7). The psalm ends with a prayer for the nation: “Save Your people and bless Your inheritance; shepherd them and carry them forever” (v.9).
context.custom: Israelites prayed standing, with hands lifted up toward the sanctuary (1 Kings 8:22; Lamentations 2:19). The “holy sanctuary” (v.2) is the inner room of the tabernacle or Temple, the Most Holy Place where the ark stood. The Pit was the grave, the realm of the dead.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 29 hears the voice of the LORD in a thunderstorm.
context.timelineBible: Paul writes that the Lord “will repay each one according to his deeds” (Romans 2:6), as v.4 asks. The shepherd-king who carries his people (v.9) is the picture of Isaiah 40:11 and of Jesus carrying the lost sheep on His shoulders (Luke 15:5).

translation.meaning: A pit, cistern, dungeon; the grave.
The inner room of the sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.

gospelParallels.note: God will repay each one according to his deeds.
He joyfully puts the sheep on his shoulders.
Men everywhere should pray, lifting up holy hands.

otBackground.note: Solomon spreads his hands toward heaven.
He carries the lambs in His arms.
You, O LORD, are a shield around me.

overview.summary: David pleads with God not to be silent, then blesses Him for hearing, calling Him his strength and shield, and prays that God will shepherd His people forever.
overview.settingLine: Hands lifted toward the Most Holy Place.

history.t: The inner room of God’s house.

archaeology.t: Plastered pits stored water and sometimes held prisoners (Jeremiah 38:6).
Temples at Ain Dara and Tell Tayinat have the same three rooms as Solomon’s Temple.

overview.discussion: Some “speak peace… while malice is in their hearts” (v.3). Where do my words and my heart not match?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (1-125 in the app so far). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: David
